name: A Game Still Being Played Can Be Resumed
note: Started 2026-10-01 with the killer section (5); the older sections had no manifest and still have none. Section 6 (the seconds played, BACKLOG D15) added 2026-10-08.

mutations.name: a killer save is offered without its cages
mutations.why: Resumed, the board is a near-empty grid with no cages and no rule that pins it down; the player is handed an unsolvable classic puzzle.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer save without its cages must not be offered

mutations.name: a cage set that leaves cells out passes
mutations.why: Cells outside every cage get no outline and no sum; the puzzle the player sees is not the one that was generated.
mutations.expectFailure: cages that leave cells out are not a killer

mutations.name: a cell may sit in two cages
mutations.why: Two outlines claim the same cell; the sums no longer describe one grid.
mutations.find: if (!Number.isInteger(cell) || cell < 0 || cell > 80 || seen.has(cell)) return false;
mutations.expectFailure: a cell in two places is not a cage set

mutations.name: a resumed game's seconds played start again
mutations.why: Survival is graded on the seconds played: a game resumed half-way would be graded on its second half alone — S+ for a slow game.
mutations.expectFailure: brings them back as they were

mutations.name: an old Survival save takes its time left for the time played
mutations.why: A Survival game saved before the update would come back with "seconds played" = the time left — any number at all.

mutations.name: an old Survival save counts wrong cells as right
mutations.why: A wrong digit gave no 7 s; counting it makes the worked-back time longer than was played.
mutations.find: ? board.reduce((n, row, r) => n + row.filter((v, c) => initial[r][c] === 0 && v === solution[r][c]).length, 0)
mutations.replace: ? board.reduce((n, row, r) => n + row.filter((v, c) => initial[r][c] === 0 && v !== 0).length, 0)

mutations.name: the old-save bonus drifts from the game's
mutations.why: If the game ever gives a different bonus, old saves would be worked back with the wrong one.

mutations.name: the save leaves the seconds played out
mutations.why: Every resumed game would be an "old save" again: Survival worked back from the board, the rest restarted from the clock.
mutations.expectFailure: the saved game must carry the seconds played

mutations.name: resume puts back only the clock
mutations.why: The seconds played would keep whatever the last game left — or 0 after a relaunch.
mutations.find: resetTimer(saved.level, saved.gameMode, saved);   // the clock and the seconds played
mutations.expectFailure: resuming must put back both clocks

mutations.name: the timer ignores a saved game's seconds played
mutations.why: A resumed game would start its seconds played at 0.
mutations.expectFailure: must take a saved game's seconds played
